title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous pages: X is a variety over a field K, with K finitely generated over Q in the cancelled passage. Γ = Gal(K̄/K) acts on the profinite fundamental groupoid Π̂_1(X_K̄) by transport of structure. By (28), ^{uv}l = ^u(^v l).

For a path l : x → y, define two maps on Γ by
  ^u l = l · f_l(u) = g_l(u) · l,
so that f_l(u) = l^{-1}·^u l lies in π̂_1(X,x) and g_l(u) = ^u l·l^{-1} lies in π̂_1(X,y). The previous page derived the cocycle identities
  f_l(uv) = f_l(u)·^u f_l(v)   and   g_l(uv) = ^u g_l(v)·g_l(u).
Thus f_l is a right 1-cocycle and g_l^{-1} is a left 1-cocycle; Grothendieck's notation H^1_dr means 'à droite', i.e. right cocycles.

This page. When x and y are K-rational, Γ acts on π̂_1(X,x) and π̂_1(X,y), and l serves as an 'origin' element of the path set. Now change the path: l' = la = bl, with a ∈ π_1(X,x) and b ∈ π_1(X,y). Using (10)-(11), this gives (31):
  f_{l'}(u) = a^{-1} f_l(u) ^u a,
  g_{l'}(u) = ^u b g_l(u) b^{-1},
equivalently g_{l'}^{-1}(u) = b g_l^{-1}(u) ^u b^{-1}.
So the cohomology classes do not depend on the path chosen. One obtains (32):
  g_{y,x} ∈ H^1(Γ, π̂_1(X,y))   and   f_{y,x} ∈ H^1_dr(Γ, π̂_1(X,x)).
These two classes correspond under the canonical outer isomorphism π̂_1(X,x) ≅ π̂_1(X,y).

The diagonal margin note says:
- the cochains f_l, g_l and the formulas (31) make sense for any path in the profinite groupoid;
- defining the classes (32) needs x and y to be K-rational, since otherwise Γ does not act on the vertex groups.

In modern terms, these are the classes of the Γ-equivariant path torsor (bitorsor) π̂_1(X; x,y). For fixed base point x, the assignment y ↦ [π̂_1(X;x,y)] ∈ H^1(Γ, π̂_1(X_K̄,x)) is the non-abelian Kummer map (Grothendieck's 'section map' X(K) → {sections}/conjugacy).

The cancelled paragraph, picked up again on p.79, begins a remark: if K is of finite type over Q and X embeds in a semi-abelian variety (an abelian variety extended by a torus), then Mordell–Weil implies something about these classes for fixed x_0. The natural reading is that the abelianized classes are Kummer classes of y − x_0 in a finitely generated group. Page 79 ends this with 'bidon', apparently dismissing it.
errors: No mathematical error. Both formulas in (31) check: from ^u(la) = l f_l(u) ^u a = (la)·a^{-1} f_l(u) ^u a, and similarly for g.

Minor sign-convention point: g_l satisfies g(uv) = ^u g(v) g(u), so it is g_l^{-1}, not g_l, that is a cocycle in the usual sense. The page states the class 'g_{y,x} ∈ H^1' loosely; the previous page gets this right.
Notational slip in the final line: π̂_1(Y,y) should be π̂_1(X,y).
On this page a and b are written in the discrete π_1, while the classes live in profinite groups. The margin note itself says that arbitrary paths in Π̂_1 are allowed.

ideas.what: Cocycles f_l and g_l attached to a path between rational points; their classes are independent of the path (31)-(32)
ideas.modern_name: Class of the étale path torsor in non-abelian H^1(Γ, π_1); non-abelian Kummer map / section map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, Esquisse 1984); later Nakamura, Mochizuki, and Minhyong Kim (unipotent version, 2005)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27.6.1983), section conjecture: rational points give conjugacy classes of sections of π_1(X) → Γ

ideas.what: Left and right cocycles corresponding to the two sides of the bitorsor π̂_1(X;x,y), related by the outer isomorphism; the earlier margin asks for explicit 'bicocycles'
ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian H^1 of bitorsors; Γ-equivariant fundamental groupoid
ideas.where_published: Bitorsor formalism appears in Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne; not specifically in this Galois-groupoid form in Grothendieck's published texts

ideas.what: Abandoned remark: for X embedded in a semi-abelian variety over a finitely generated K, Mordell–Weil constrains the classes for fixed x_0
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of the non-abelian Kummer map with the abelian Kummer map on the Albanese (generalized Jacobian); finite generation used as in Chabauty–Kim
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Kummer theory of abelian varieties); non-abelian refinement by Minhyong Kim (2005-2009)

missed.claim: Grothendieck began, crossed out, and then partly dismissed ('bidon') a remark linking the path-torsor classes to the Mordell–Weil group, via an embedding of X in a semi-abelian variety. This anticipates the abelianized Kummer map underlying Chabauty-type and Kim-type arguments, but is not carried further.
missed.quote: Le théorème de Mordell-Weil implique que si K est un corps de type fini sur Q ... et si X peut se plonger dans un groupe algébrique ext. d'une VA par un tore, alors pour x_0 fixé,
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mainly historical. It shows that the non-abelian Kummer map, and its relation to Mordell–Weil through the abelianization, were already on Grothendieck's mind in these notes (dated from 1978 on), probably before the 1983 Faltings letter. The mathematics is now standard through Kim's work.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine non-abelian cohomology computation constructing the classes of étale path torsors, which is the standard section-conjecture framework. The only point of interest is a cancelled, unfinished remark connecting these classes to Mordell–Weil for subvarieties of semi-abelian varieties. That is historically suggestive of later Kim-type ideas, but it is not developed.
transcription_corrections: 'H^1_dr' means right cocycles ('à droite'), not de Rham.

In (31) the underbrace under f_a(u) is a^{-1}·^u a and the one under g_b(u) is ^u b·b^{-1}. The struck-through underbrace under g_ℓ(u) is illegible and partly struck through, so not clearly ^u l·l^{-1}.

Margin reading is plausibly: 'Les f_ℓ(u), g_ℓ(u) sont définis (et les formules (31) valables) pour un chemin ℓ: x → y quelconque dans le groupoïde Π̂_1(X). Par contre, la définition des classes de cohomologie (32) dépend de ce que x, y soient des points rationnels sur K ...'
